startup_idea:
Voice-First AI Assistant for Local MSMEs is a mobile startup that builds local-language, voice-driven AI tools to help small shopkeepers and micro-businesses in India automate daily tasks like inventory tracking, GST record-keeping, and customer follow-ups via WhatsApp and UPI.

The Problem

Millions of small shopkeepers, grocers, and local vendors (MSMEs) run vital parts of the economy, yet they struggle with complex digital software, typing in English, or managing manual ledger books. Existing tools are too complicated or require computer literacy they do not have.

The Solution

• Voice-First Interface: Shopkeepers speak in regional languages (like Hindi, Marathi, or Gujarati) to log sales, check stock, or draft supplier messages.
• WhatsApp & UPI Integration: The AI agent operates directly inside WhatsApp or links with UPI payment alerts to automatically reconcile daily cash flows.
• Automated Compliance: It generates basic digital invoices and flags low-stock items without manual data entry.

seven_day_plan: Day 1: Identify and recruit 30 shopkeepers for interviews in Mumbai.
Day 2: Conduct 30 in‑person interviews focusing on pain points and willingness to use voice.
Day 3: Build a low‑fidelity voice prototype using existing ASR APIs.
Day 4: Set up a landing page with WhatsApp sign‑up and a ₹200 subscription CTA.
Day 5: Run a small paid ad campaign on Facebook targeting local markets.
Day 6: Collect feedback from interviewees and refine prototype.
Day 7: Prepare data for pilot selection.
thirty_day_plan: Day 8: Launch concierge MVP with 20 pilot users in Mumbai.
Day 9-10: Onboard pilot users and provide training on voice logging.
Day 11-15: Monitor usage, collect daily logs, and troubleshoot.
Day 16-20: Run a pricing test: offer 1‑month free trial to 50 shopkeepers in Pune.
Day 21-25: Analyze pilot data, compute CAC and conversion.
Day 26-30: Iterate on voice accuracy based on feedback and prepare for scaling.
ninety_day_plan: Day 31-35: Expand pilot to 50 shopkeepers across 3 cities.
Day 36-40: Track retention rates, churn, and feature usage.
Day 41-45: Conduct a regulatory compliance audit for invoicing and data handling.
Day 46-50: Optimize pricing model based on willingness data.
Day 51-55: Release first stable version with automated invoice generation.
Day 56-60: Evaluate unit economics (LTV, CAC) and decide on scaling vs pivot.
Day 61-90: Build marketing funnel, partner with local associations, and refine product roadmap.
